subject: QBR prep: April KPI synthesis + action items (latency, cost, uptime)
messages:
From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.ai>
To: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>, Ava Chen <ava.chen@redwood.ai>, Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.ai>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 2 May 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: QBR prep: April KPI synthesis + action items (latency, cost, uptime)

Team —

Attached is the April KPI dashboard export for PriorityHealth and a short synthesis of notable signals. We're consolidating for the QBR next Friday (05/08). Please review and add any blockers or suggested slides by EOD Monday so I can finalize the deck. High-level notes: 

- Latency: 95p latency increased ~18% week over week around 4/12–4/16. Initial look points to a routing change that increased cold-starts on dedicated pools.
- Cost: Token spend up 12% month over month; effective cost/token rose ~6% driven by re-generated completions on a small subset of high-retry prompts.
- Uptime: Service-level uptime for the account is 99.92% (monthly), two brief incidents during maintenance windows logged on 4/14 and 4/21.
- Usage: Steady growth in peak concurrency; recommend verifying autoscale headroom for dedicated pool during May promotions.

Action items I propose:
1) Markus to confirm whether the routing policy change on 4/10 could explain latency spike and propose rollback or soft-fallback.
2) Ava to produce a per-route cost breakdown and flag top 5 prompts that generate most re-runs.
3) Rachel to pull SRE incident postmortems and confirm exact MTTR and RCA summaries for the two maintenance events.
4) Stephanie to draft a brief SLA note for the QBR highlighting mitigation and credits if applicable.

Attachments: April_KPI_dashboard.pdf (summary export).

Ping me in thread if you need access to the raw dashboards. I will loop in the PriorityHealth contact after we solidify the talking points.

Thanks,
Evelyn
Evelyn Hart
Director, Customer Success — Redwood Inference
[evelyn.hart@redwood.ai]  |  +1 (415) 555-0173

From: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.ai>
Cc: Ava Chen <ava.chen@redwood.ai>, Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 3 May 2026 10:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: QBR prep: April KPI synthesis + action items (latency, cost, uptime)

On Sat, May 2, 2026 at 9:12 AM Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.ai> wrote:
> Team —
> Attached is the April KPI dashboard export for PriorityHealth...

Quick read —
- I dug into the routing logs around 4/12–4/16. We had a policy change that started preferring the new lower-cost pool (dedicated-pool-3) for mid-length sequences. That pool has a smaller warm buffer and no pre-warm on scale events; result: higher cold-start tail.
- Recommendation: revert preference for the lower-cost pool for production routes serving PriorityHealth OR enable pre-warm for that pool for peak hours. Revert is fastest; pre-warm is more sustainable.

I'll prepare a short comparison export (latency by pool + cost delta) and attach by EOD. If we revert, ops will need a 30-minute maintenance window.

Markus
VP, Serving Infrastructure

From: Ava Chen <ava.chen@redwood.ai>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.ai>, Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>
Cc: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.ai>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 3 May 2026 14:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: QBR prep: April KPI synthesis + action items (latency, cost, uptime)

Thanks — attached a quick per-route cost export and a notes sheet (KPI_notes_20260503.xlsx). Highlights below: 

- Top 5 cost drivers for PriorityHealth: session-retry loop on the claims-reconciliation route (~28% of token spend), long-context embeddings use for historical search (~18%), high volume of short responses (amortized overhead), frequent streaming sessions (overhead + tokens), and a small number of large-batch reruns for testing.
- For the retry loop I flagged two prompts that re-generate on server-side validation; suggests a prompt-level fix or a client-side de-dup dedupe check.
- I added a suggested slide: "Cost by route (April) — proposed mitigations" with before/after cost projections if we apply prompt fixes and routing revert.

Attachment: KPI_notes_20260503.xlsx (per-route export + mitigation estimates).

Ava
Senior Product Analyst, Redwood Inference

From: Tom Sweeney <tom.sweeney@priorityhealth.com>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.ai>
Cc: PriorityHealth Billing <billing@priorityhealth.com>
Date: Mon, 4 May 2026 09:41:00 -0700
Subject: Re: QBR prep: April KPI synthesis + action items (latency, cost, uptime)

Evelyn —

Thanks for the dashboard. A couple of quick questions ahead of the QBR: 
1) The cost breakdown is helpful — can you confirm whether the token cost shown includes penalty billing for retries? Our billing team is seeing a mismatch versus the invoice.
2) SLA: you noted two maintenance events — would that qualify for any service credit? We track incident windows for our compliance.

Also, if you have a one-slide explanation of the latency spike root cause and proposed timeline to remediate that would help us explain to our operations folks. Can you send by Tuesday?

Thanks,
Tom Sweeney
Director of Integrations — PriorityHealth

From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.ai>
To: Tom Sweeney <tom.sweeney@priorityhealth.com>
Cc: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>, Ava Chen <ava.chen@redwood.ai>, Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.ai>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 4 May 2026 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: QBR prep: April KPI synthesis + action items (latency, cost, uptime)

Tom —

Thanks for the quick read. Short answers: 
- Cost: The export in the dashboard includes raw token accounting plus internal retry counts. The invoice shows billed units after our retry de-duplication policy; I asked Ava to include a reconciled view in KPI_notes_20260503.xlsx (tab: billing-reconcile). That should explain the mismatch — I'll confirm numbers with Billing and loop back by EOD.
- SLA credit: Rachel and I reviewed the incidents; both were scheduled maintenance windows that impacted a small subset of PriorityHealth workers. Our SLA (section 4.2) provides for credit evaluation for downtime exceeding monthly thresholds — Rachel will finalize the MTTR/RCA and eligibility for credit.

Markus has proposed two remediation options for latency (revert routing or pre-warm). Markus: can you confirm estimated timeline and ops impact? If revert, we can announce a 30-minute window during off-peak and should see the 95p tail normalize within one business day. If pre-warm, ops needs a config change and load testing and we'd expect partial improvement in 48–72 hours.

I'll draft the one-slide causality + timeline now and send separately; plan to share the finished QBR deck and the signed slide with PriorityHealth on Wednesday morning.

Best,
Evelyn

From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.ai>
To: Tom Sweeney <tom.sweeney@priorityhealth.com>, PriorityHealth Billing <billing@priorityhealth.com>
Cc: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>, Ava Chen <ava.chen@redwood.ai>, Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.ai>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 5 May 2026 16:42:00 -0700
Subject: Final QBR materials: QBR_deck_v3.pptx + short summary slide

Tom / PriorityHealth team —

Thanks for the earlier questions. Attached is the finalized QBR deck (QBR_deck_v3.pptx) and a separate single-slide summary that explains the latency root cause, remediation plan, and estimated timeline. Quick summary: 

- Root cause: routing preference that shifted a portion of production traffic to a lower-cost pool with limited warm buffer, increasing cold-start tail latency.
- Remediation: we reverted the routing preference at 14:00 PDT on 05/05; observed 95p latency drop back to baseline within 6 hours during ramp verification.
- Billing reconciliation: Ava attached the reconciled billing tab. We will issue any eligible SLA credits as per section 4.2; Rachel is producing the formal incident report.

Next steps / who owns what: 
- Rachel: incident report + credit eligibility (deliverable: 5/06 COB).
- Ava: final per-route cost sheet + recommended prompt fixes (deliverable: 5/06 COB).
- Markus: confirm whether pre-warm should be enabled for peak hours and provide ops runbook (deliverable: 5/12).
- Evelyn / Stephanie: finalize QBR meeting logistics and slide deck distribution (we'll use the link below).

Doc link: https://redwood.app/dashboards/PH-Q2-KPIs
Signed deck link: https://app.redwood.com/signed/PH-QBR-deck-v3

If you confirm receipt, we'll schedule the QBR for Friday (05/08) at 10:00 AM PT.

Best regards,
Evelyn Hart
Director, Customer Success — Redwood Inference
Attachments: QBR_deck_v3.pptx (deck), April_KPI_dashboard.pdf (attached earlier), KPI_notes_20260503.xlsx
